newsitem.title: CHINA: China region to open up farmland to foreign funds.
newsitem.headline: China region to open up farmland to foreign funds.

text.p: Officials in China's northwestern Xinjiang region have opened state-owned farming land to foreign investment, the Publication Digest said on Thursday.
The Xinjiang Planning Commission said on September 1 it would try to attract overseas investors to cultivate 16,000 hectares (39,600 acres) of prime farmland, the newspaper said.
"We welcome investors from any country or region to grow grain, cotton or other crops on this land," the report quoted Hu Guoxuan, vice-director of the Planning Commission, as saying.
Investors would also be allowed to develop breeding, processing and tourism on the land, Hu said.

Of the land being offered, 9,300 hectares (23,000 acres) was prime cropland north of the Tianshan Mountains while the remainder could be chosen by investors, the digest said. One-fifth of the land had been cultivated previously and the rest was undeveloped, the newspaper said.

Beijing, faced with growing popular dissatisfaction over a widening economic gap between the booming coastal regions and central and western provinces, is trying to encourage foreign investment in the hinterland.
